newsitem.title: USA: Ad campaign opposes Con Edison settlement.
newsitem.headline: Ad campaign opposes Con Edison settlement.

text.p: A group called New Yorkers for Energy Choice begins an advertising campaign Tuesday aimed at gaining changes in Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc's restructuring settlement with New York regulators, a spokeswoman for the group told Reuters Monday.
Nancy Klein said the effort wilreprinting the paper's editorial opposing the settlement.
Future ads will reprint an opposing editorial from Gannett Co Inc's Suburban Newspapers, she said. These papers cover Con Edison's Westchester County service area north of New York City.

Describing those funding the campaign as "the left outs," Klein said it will also include radio and television advertisements pointing out "proposals across the (Hudson) River" from Public Service Electric & Gas offering to allow all customers access to the competitive power market.
Con Edison's settlement proposes phasing access in over five years and limits rate cuts for most businesses to 10 percent, while offering manufacturers a 25 percent cut.
Klein said all the adds will urge those opposed to the settlement to call Governor Pataki and provide his toll-free phone number.

She said many New Yorkers for Energy Choice members were intervenors in the Con Edison settlement, including the Independent Power Producers of New York Inc; Wheeled Electric Power and the Food Industry Alliance, a state-wide supermarkets group; and Housing Services Inc, which represents cooperative housing projects.
Klein pointed out that none of the power users in the group would bnenefit from the biggest rate cuts proposed by the Con Edison settlement.

In June, a New York Public Service Commission law judge recommended more negotiations between Con Edison and the intervenors, saying the settlement the utility reached with the commission staff "does not sufficently remove competitive barriers."

Klein said members of the new group report there were some talks in addition to the briefs filed in response the the law judge's recommendations. The deadline for filing those briefs was Friday, July 25.
During the limited talks, she continued, Con Edison officials resisted any changes in the settlement, describing it as "finely tuned" and "comprehensive."
